hook: SCP-1173 concerns a country that may or may not exist, and the less you know going in, the better it works. Read the description as a careful account of a delusion, and keep track of who is said to hold it. The final addendum changes who the document is talking to.
whyItMatters: It is a memetic file where the hazard is not death or obvious madness but a competing picture of the world, complete with history, literature and news coverage. The trigger is a line of ordinary small talk, which makes the spread feel plausible. The containment procedures already hint that the problem reaches inside the Foundation, which is why they read so oddly cautious.
thingsToNotice: Addendum 1173-1 reveals that infection runs through every level of the Foundation, that infected units deliberately spread it, and that armed clashes between units stopped only with Protocol 1173-Omicron, a truce between two camps of roughly equal size. The final message then addresses you directly: hidden keyword tests have judged you uninfected, so you are drafted into a covert resistance whose job is to isolate colleagues, probe what they know about Samothrace and dose them with Class O amnestic. The text never settles whether the IDAS is a delusion or something the uninfected cannot see, and details such as the 1709 image caption, the old literary references and more than 800 schizophrenic patients recalling a U.S. war there keep nudging toward the less comfortable reading. If the country is real, the cure amounts to one half of the Foundation quietly wiping the other half's knowledge while the infected still trust the truce. Six Overseers sign the message, which hints at how far up the split goes.
